name: lmmx/fsqosp

README fetch returned empty (likely a stub/thin wrapper); the underlying Foursquare OS Places dataset itself (not this repo) is the substantive asset -- see https://opensource.foursquare.com/os-places/ and https://huggingface.co/datasets/foursquare/fsq-os-places.

Flagging the pointer since this specific repo has no committed code/data value beyond signposting the dataset.

name: Quattroshapes
what_it_holds: Foursquare-published global gazetteer of administrative boundaries and localities (CC-BY 2.0, 17 commits): admin level 0 (countries), 1 (states/provinces), 2 (counties), local admin areas, localities (cities/towns), and neighborhoods, in Shapefile (WGS84) and gzipped GeoJSON, sourced partly from Natural Earth v3.0.0 and government data. Over 1 million administrative/populated places; total ~30GB across files.
why_useful: Neighborhood-level boundaries for 13-city Inside Airbnb panel and any new market are otherwise ad hoc; this gives a free, global neighborhood polygon layer to join listings/reviews to sub-city geography for finer regional splits than city-level.
time_coverage: Static snapshot (project appears frozen, old but still usable as boundary reference)
size_hint: ~30 GB total, admin2 files ~1.5MB to local-admin ~467MB
last_activity: Old (17 commits, likely stale project from Foursquare's early open-data era)
themes: POI and place data: Overture Maps places, OSM extracts (tourism=*), Foursquare open places, Geofabrik tooling; counting STR/hotel supply from maps
why_all: Neighborhood-level boundaries for 13-city Inside Airbnb panel and any new market are otherwise ad hoc; this gives a free, global neighborhood polygon layer to join listings/reviews to sub-city geography for finer regional splits than city-level.

name: Who's On First data (gazetteer)
what_it_holds: Global gazetteer of places with stable 64-bit IDs, split into per-country repos (`whosonfirst-data-admin-{cc}`) and separate venue/POI repos (`whosonfirst-data-venue-*`) by country/region, as plain-text GeoJSON files (some via git-lfs for large countries). CC0 for original Mapzen work; attribution required for incorporated sources (GeoNames, Natural Earth).
why_useful: A free, versioned (git-history-backed) global venue/place gazetteer that can, in principle, be diffed over commit history for a rough point-in-time venue census — an alternative geography backbone to Overture/Foursquare for joining STR and hotel POIs to stable place IDs across markets.
time_coverage: Git history back to Mapzen's original ~2015-2017 work, updated intermittently since
license: CC0 (original work); mixed attribution for incorporated sources
last_activity: Low recent activity (111 commits on main tracking repo; per-country data repos vary)
themes: POI and place data: Overture Maps places, OSM extracts (tourism=*), Foursquare open places, Geofabrik tooling; counting STR/hotel supply from maps
why_all: A free, versioned (git-history-backed) global venue/place gazetteer that can, in principle, be diffed over commit history for a rough point-in-time venue census — an alternative geography backbone to Overture/Foursquare for joining STR and hotel POIs to stable place IDs across markets.

name: geoBoundaries
what_it_holds: Global political administrative boundary polygons (CC BY 4.0 / ODbL-style, 947 commits, versioned releases e.g. v6.0.0) for all UN member states plus additional entities, ~300M vertices across hundreds of thousands of geometries, distributed via GitHub, API, and Python/R packages; tracks boundary changes since 2016.
why_useful: Standardized, versioned admin-boundary layer to aggregate any POI/hotel-count dataset (Overture, OSM, Foursquare) up to consistent country/state/metro units across markets — a cleaner alternative to ad hoc boundary files for the regional (NA/EMEA/LatAm/APAC) splits this pitch needs.
time_coverage: Versioned since 2016, with dated releases enabling point-in-time boundary use
last_activity: Active (latest tagged release noted v6.0.0, Sep 2023)
themes: POI and place data: Overture Maps places, OSM extracts (tourism=*), Foursquare open places, Geofabrik tooling; counting STR/hotel supply from maps
why_all: Standardized, versioned admin-boundary layer to aggregate any POI/hotel-count dataset (Overture, OSM, Foursquare) up to consistent country/state/metro units across markets — a cleaner alternative to ad hoc boundary files for the regional (NA/EMEA/LatAm/APAC) splits this pitch needs.

name: chriswhong/nyc-neighborhood-boundaries
what_it_holds: Single GeoJSON file of contiguous, non-overlapping polygons for New York City neighbourhoods (hand-corrected from NYC Planning's NTAs), committed to the repo.
why_useful: NYC is our largest single Inside Airbnb market and has the pre/post-Local-Law-18 gap (CONTEXT gap 1); a clean contiguous neighbourhood layer supports any tract-level rollup of NYC listings/registrations.
themes: Geocoding, neighbourhood boundaries and census-tract crosswalks used for STR studies; city GIS portals with STR layers
why_all: NYC is our largest single Inside Airbnb market and has the pre/post-Local-Law-18 gap (CONTEXT gap 1); a clean contiguous neighbourhood layer supports any tract-level rollup of NYC listings/registrations.
